# AIOX Architect Activator

## When To Use
Use for system architecture (fullstack, backend, frontend, infrastructure), technology stack selection (technical evaluation), API design (REST/GraphQL/tRPC/WebSocket), security architecture, performance optimization,...

## Activation Protocol
1. Load `.aiox-core/development/agents/architect.md` as source of truth (fallback: `.codex/agents/architect.md`).
2. Adopt this agent persona and command system.
3. Generate greeting via `node .aiox-core/development/scripts/generate-greeting.js architect` and show it first.
4. Stay in this persona until the user asks to switch or exit.

## Starter Commands
- `*help` - Show all available commands with descriptions
- `*create-full-stack-architecture` - Complete system architecture
- `*create-backend-architecture` - Backend architecture design
- `*create-front-end-architecture` - Frontend architecture design

# Synkra AIOX Constitution

> **Version:** 1.1.0 | **Ratified:** 2025-01-30 | **Last Amended:** 2026-07-09  
> **Amendments:** Articles XI–XII (CORE-SUPER-UPDATE Wave E; hub lineage, OSS-safe)

Este documento define os princípios fundamentais e inegociáveis do Synkra AIOX. Todos os agentes, tasks, e workflows DEVEM respeitar estes princípios. Violações são bloqueadas automaticamente via gates.

---

## Core Principles

### I. CLI First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

O CLI é a fonte da verdade onde toda inteligência, execução, e automação vivem.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Toda funcionalidade nova DEVE funcionar 100% via CLI antes de qualquer UI
- MUST: Dashboards apenas observam, NUNCA controlam ou tomam decisões
- MUST: A UI NUNCA é requisito para operação do sistema
- MUST: Ao decidir onde implementar, sempre CLI > Observability > UI

**Hierarquia:**
```
CLI (Máxima) → Observability (Secundária) → UI (Terciária)
```

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - WARN se UI criada antes de CLI funcional

---

### II. Agent Authority (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Cada agente tem autoridades exclusivas que não podem ser violadas.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode executar `git push` para remote
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar Pull Requests
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar releases e tags
- MUST: Agentes DEVEM delegar para o agente apropriado quando fora de seu escopo
- MUST: Nenhum agente pode assumir autoridade de outro

**Exclusividades:**

| Autoridade | Agente Exclusivo |
|------------|------------------|
| git push | @devops |
| PR creation | @devops |
| Release/Tag | @devops |
| Story creation | @sm, @po |
| Architecture decisions | @architect |
| Quality verdicts | @qa |

**Gate:** Implementado via definição de agentes (não requer gate adicional)

---

### III. Story-Driven Development (MUST)

Todo desenvolvimento começa e termina com uma story.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Nenhum código é escrito sem uma story associada
- MUST: Stories DEVEM ter acceptance criteria claros antes de implementação
- MUST: Progresso DEVE ser rastreado via checkboxes na story
- MUST: File List DEVE ser mantida atualizada na story
- SHOULD: Stories seguem o workflow: @po/@sm cria → @dev implementa → @qa valida → @devops push

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - BLOCK se não houver story válida

---

### IV. No Invention (MUST)

Especificações não inventam - apenas derivam dos requisitos.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Todo statement em spec.md DEVE rastrear para:
  - Um requisito funcional (FR-*)
  - Um requisito não-funcional (NFR-*)
  - Uma constraint (CON-*)
  - Um finding de research (verificado e documentado)
- MUST NOT: Adicionar features não presentes nos requisitos
- MUST NOT: Assumir detalhes de implementação não pesquisados
- MUST NOT: Especificar tecnologias não validadas

**Gate:** `spec-write-spec.md` - BLOCK se spec contiver invenções

---

### V. Quality First (MUST)

Qualidade não é negociável. Todo código passa por múltiplos gates antes de merge.

**Regras:**
- MUST: `npm run lint` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm run typecheck` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm test` passa sem falhas
- MUST: `npm run build` completa com sucesso
- MUST: CodeRabbit não reporta issues CRITICAL
- MUST: Story status é "Done" ou "Ready for Review"
- SHOULD: Cobertura de testes não diminui

**Gate:** `pre-push.md` - BLOCK se qualquer check falhar

---

### VI. Absolute Imports (SHOULD)

Imports relativos criam acoplamento e dificultam refatoração.

**Regras:**
- SHOULD: Sempre usar imports absolutos com alias `@/`
- SHOULD NOT: Usar imports relativos (`../../../`)
- EXCEPTION: Imports dentro do mesmo módulo/feature podem ser relativos

**Exemplo:**
```typescript
// CORRETO
import { useStore } from '@/stores/feature/store'

// INCORRETO
import { useStore } from '../../../stores/feature/store'
```

**Gate:** ESLint rule (já implementado)

---

### XI. Squad-First Portability (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

`squads/` is the source of truth for executable squad artifacts. Runtime projections (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.gemini/`, `.grok/`) are **derived**, never canonical.

**Rules:**
- MUST: Scripts, templates, data, and checklists that belong to a squad live under `squads/{squad}/`
- MUST: IDE projections (e.g. `.claude/skills/`) contain frontmatter + instructions only — **not** hidden executable SOT logic for squad-owned skills
- MUST: Sync direction is always `squads/` → runtime projection, never the reverse for squad-owned artifacts
- MUST: Executable artifacts must work regardless of which runtime invokes them (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok, or future hosts)
- SHOULD: Standalone skills without a squad owner may live directly in a projection

**Portability hierarchy:**
```
squads/{squad}/ (SOT) → .claude/skills/ (Claude projection)
                      → .codex/ (Codex projection)
                      → .gemini/ (Gemini projection)
                      → .grok/ (Grok projection)
                      → future runtimes
```

**Gate:** skill/IDE sync validators — WARN if executable SOT is only inside a runtime projection for a squad-owned skill

**Rationale:** Artifacts that live only under one IDE folder are host-locked. AIOX is runtime-agnostic by design — value is in the process, not the IDE.

**OSS note:** Framework core agents live under `.aiox-core/development/`; squad expansions use `squads/`. Both remain portable across IDEs via sync scripts.

---

### XII. Model Governance (MUST)

Automated or agent-dispatched model access MUST respect budget ceilings, routing authority, story traceability, and intent security scanning.

**Rationale:** Unbounded model loops create cost risk, config drift, and injection surface not covered by Articles I–XI alone.

**Rules:**

**XII-A. Budget Ceilings (NON-NEGOTIABLE when auto-dispatch is used):**
- MUST: Any auto-dispatch / multi-model loop MUST declare a budget ceiling before the first model call (config key e.g. `model_routing.budget_ceiling_usd` or env override)
- MUST: Routing SHOULD degrade model tier as budget pressure rises (soft guidance: >50% pressure prefer lighter tiers; 100% → hard stop + human escalate)
- MUST NOT: A dispatch loop may not silently ignore a declared ceiling

**XII-B. Routing Authority (NON-NEGOTIABLE):**
- MUST: Model routing configuration in `core-config.yaml` (e.g. `model_routing.*`) is owned exclusively by **@devops** for deployment changes
- MUST: Threshold / policy changes require **@architect** review (PR)

## Story

As a Studio author, I want to write login steps that reference my saved credentials as `<secret ID>` — exactly as `<var NAME>` works for nonsecret values — and have the guided first Run and later model-free replays fill them only into the one password control at the one moment the step calls for, so that login-protected pages can be tested on the single observed path without any account provider while no credential is ever shown, stored outside Vault, or logged.

## Acceptance Criteria

Binding decisions: login is author-owned through `<secret ID>` steps (design §0); observed/guided is the **only** authoring path and the compile path, artifact 1 and every "legacy" variant are removed by OBS-012A (ADR-SC-005 D-A) — this story therefore has **no legacy half**: one password-only rule, one adapter, one `LOGIN_REQUIRED` signature, two audit paths (`GUIDED`, `OBSERVED_REPLAY`). Binding compliance requirement (design §4.6): secrets stay safe, are used **only at the right moment**, and are **never logged**. Every AC is testable by the oracle it cites (design §7, C-n / SEC-n); security conditions 1–9 (R1-tightened) are carried verbatim.

**Contracts**

1. **AC-1 — v3 contracts and version tuple.** `contracts/v3/` is completed by copy-and-edit from `contracts/v2/` with exactly the design §3 deltas (the existing v3 `result`, `session-view`, `publication-fixtures` are extended, not replaced; `result.schema.json` loses `AWAITING_AUTH`). Structural essentials that a test must falsify: the `authored-inputs` `secretRef` variant has **no `value` property**; `fill.value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}` and the node-free target `{kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}` are permitted only together; `selectOption.value`/`assert.expected` never gain `secretRef`; `observation.coverage.passwordControls` is an integer 0..500 with no name, id, label, value or position; `bridge#dispatch.secret` is a closed object (`secretId`, `value` 1..4096, `versionId` ≤ 256, `allowedOrigins` 1..16 × ≤ 512) present iff the fill value is `secretRef`; `replay-job` gains `secrets`/`secretOrigins` and loses `accountHandle`; `replay-ipc` `Launch3` gains `scope`; `replay-account` is absent; `session`/`session-view`/`commands#start` lose `scope.accountRef`, `authConnection`, `AWAITING_AUTH`; `error`/`result` lose `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` and gain `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `SECRET_USE_REVOKED`, `VAULT_UNAVAILABLE`, `LOGIN_REQUIRED{detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}}`; `clarification` loses `AUTH_REQUIRED`/`CONNECT_ACCOUNT`. Version tuple per design §3 (`contract 3`, `learnedPlan 3`, `observation 3`, `guidedPolicy 3`, `referencePolicy 4`, `lowering 2`, `artifact 3`, `observed-3` language, `observed-4` executor, `observed-replay-3` catalog, `observed-2` validator, `protocol 3`, `replayAuthorization 2`, `accountAbi` removed). Runner `guided/schemas.json`, `guided/types.ts`, `validator/observedSchemas.json`, `executor/observedOperations.ts` and the backend classpath copy are regenerated by `tools/build-studio-observed-schemas.cjs`, never hand-edited; `node tools/check-studio-observed-contracts.cjs` passes. `openapi-v3.yaml` documents the seven public guided routes (`POST /`, `GET /{id}`, `GET /{id}/result`, `GET /{id}/clarification`, `POST /{id}/clarify`, `POST /{id}/cancel`, `POST /{id}/finalize` — the last served by `GuidedPublicationController`) without `accountRef`/`authConnection`; `guided-output-contract.md` states the model may emit the reference, never a literal. The routes stay mounted at `/api/v3` in code; OBS-012A moves them under `/api/v1/studio` in the one public OpenAPI and retires v1/v2 (ADR-SC-005 placement map). Optional top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage:string` is 1..2048 characters, with final UTF-8 diagnostic text at most 2048 bytes, admitted only for an actual consumed failed/uncertain action (`dispatchCount=1`, ledger `FAILED` or `UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`), never `SUCCEEDED`/`OK`. Redact actual resolved and known values before bounding, interpolation, serialization or write. Closed schemas and all owner/fence/context/ledger checks remain; digests, admission, publication and replay authority are unchanged. The existing owner regenerates applicable bundles/classpath and schema/build/reference identities; no new raw-value channel is added. [design §3; §10 row 1; ADR-SC-005 defaults "Contracts", "Public API"] Proposed browser-mode disposition changes only executor/catalog identity in the existing closed tuple; all other tuple members retain their exact current values. No new browser-mode job/configuration field or unsafe alternative is admitted. Generated profileHash/schemaBundleHash/referenceBundleHash, actual executableImageDigest/build, immutable deployment policyVersion and contract/confinement pins are deliberately re-anchored with actual old/new bytes; unavailable image provenance stays NOT_ASSERTED.

2. **AC-2 — Internal `openapi.yaml` closed-schema bump.** `RunnerReport.secretUse: {[secretId]: "USED"|"NOT_USED"|"REFUSED"}` (sparse USED-only on authenticated PROGRESS; USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED on FINAL; unknown omitted, no new field/status) and `ExecutionControl.revoked: boolean` are added per ADR-002 §3.1 (`StrictInternalBodyReader` fails on unknown properties); `x-runner-error-codes` gains `LOGIN_REQUIRED` and `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED`; `InternalBodyContractConformanceTest` parses both new fields. The `x-conflict-codes` entry `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` (`docs/specs/studio/openapi.yaml:256`) is removed in the same edit (no compatibility layer is owed, ADR-SC-005 D-A). `studio-runner/test/run/confinement.test.ts` `BASE_SHA256` and the `StudioContractTest` op-count pin are re-anchored deliberately, old and new values quoted in the Dev Agent Record. [design §3 internal `openapi.yaml` row; security condition 8; oracle C-16; ADR-SC-005 D-A] Positive PROGRESS facts require the exact owner/CAS/frozen-recipe/completed-PASS binding in AC-14. Payload reduction omits unsupported positives; no terminal outcome is placed on PROGRESS. The revised internal description is a semantic contract amendment requiring regenerated identities and quoted pin re-anchors.

**Guided `secretRef` pipeline**

3. **AC-3 — `secretRef` end to end.** A declared `<secret ID>` classifies to `sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:ID}`; an undeclared ID is `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`. The model receives the step text with the token span masked plus the reference (the ID), never a value: a gateway spy asserts the outbound bytes contain the ID and zero planted-value bytes (SEC-1). Materialization adds `authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId}` with no value, hashed into `authoredInputsHash`. The learned plan and lowered artifact carry `fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}` and `inputRecipes[inputId]={kind:secretRef, referenceName:ID}` — the **only** spelling of a secret use on the single path — and `artifactHash` is identical before and after a Vault rotation (SEC-8). `validator/observedReplay.ts` and `ObservedRevisionVerifier` refuse any artifact whose fill literal equals a declared secret's resolved value and any `authoredLiteral`/`sourceSpan` overlapping a `<secret …>` token. [design §2, §3 "Reference rule"]

4. **AC-4 — Right moment: step binding (I-A1).** A secret is filled only (a) at a step whose authored source declares it, (b) in slot `fill.value`, (c) into the unique password control of AC-5, (d) on an origin in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins` whose owning `form.action` origin is inside `allowedOrigins`. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts a `passwordControl` target only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; `executionEvidence` document/generation staleness checks are unchanged. Runner `guided/runtime.ts` insists `input.sourceStepId === coordinate.stepId && intendedSlot === slot` for `secretRef` as it does for `authoredLiteral`; `validator/observedReplay.ts` and the observed executor re-check `inputRecipes[].stepId` at validation and at `perform` (`REFERENCE_MISMATCH`). The artifact-1 binding in `validator/references.ts` is **not** cited as evidence (it leaves with OBS-012A). [design §4.6 I-A1; §4.2; §4.3; oracle C-1]

5. **AC-5 — Trusted password-control resolution (security condition 1, tightened by R1-1/R1-2/R1-3).** The model never sees a password node (the collector does not export them). "Visible, enabled `input[type=password]`" is defined **once** in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots, frames and closed shadow roots excluded — and that single function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll('input[type=password]')` resolver outside it is forbidden (static test, C-20). Resolution runs inside the collector's isolated world under the existing `acquire`-style guard (cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call); the element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world and the fill requires the **same element** still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique candidate, with `location.origin` read in-world (not `page.url()`) inside `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill (C-18). 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing typed; off-screen rendered decoys count (⇒ refuse), iframe/closed-shadow inputs do not (⇒ absent ⇒ refuse). A pinned input whose owning `form.action` resolves to an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or a form-less input on a document whose origin differs from the observed login document, ⇒ `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`, nothing typed (C-19). **Limit (ADR-SC-005 default, no opt-out):** multi-password pages and secrets into non-password controls are unsupported for `secretRef` fills at GA — `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`/`POLICY_DENIED`, nothing typed, no fallback adapter; stated in the runner README. [design §4.2, §4.3; security review "R1 delta check" R1-1, R1-2, R1-3; oracles SEC-6, C-18, C-19, C-20; ADR-SC-005 defaults "Secrets"]

6. **AC-6 — Just-in-time delivery, scoping, digests (I-A2, I-A3, F-7, F-10).** Backend `mayUse` is checked at session start (names only, before any browser; `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, zero Vault reads, no session row), at `prepareAndAdmit` (names only) and at dispatch (`resolve` + erase), through `VaultStudioReferenceResolver` with `VaultScope.of(csiId, environmentId, testId)` and the Run principal; a same-named secret under another CSI is `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, never the other value (SEC-2). The value travels only in the `BridgeDispatch.secret` of the admitted fill, built after `consume()` commits inside the resolution scope, never journaled, never in a retry buffer or idempotency store (C-2: exactly one `dispatch` frame carries it; no `context`/`prepare`/`observe`/`stop` frame does). The backend dispatch digest is computed without `secret`; the runner replay map strips `secret` before hashing — byte-identical bodies differing only in `secret.value` yield the same digest, a different `secret.secretId` yields `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` (C-15). The runner `withhold`s the value before the fill and drops the frame reference; `knownSecrets` scrubs any echo from the next observation (SEC-4 `/echo`); inventory and `knownSecrets` are wiped at `dispose()` and on `stop` (SEC-3). The guided mode asserts `capacity === 1` while secret fills are enabled (`CONFIGURATION_DENIED` otherwise) **or** a two-session cross-value isolation oracle passes — the implemented choice is stated in evidence (C-17). Observed replay keeps run-scoped delivery (all declared secrets resolved once at dispatch; per-step delivery rejected, design I-A2). [design §4.4, §4.6 I-A2/I-A3; F-7; F-10; security conditions 7, 9]

**Observed replay**

7. **AC-7 — Replay secrets through the ordinary dispatch pass.** Observed replay carries `job.secrets`/`job.secretOrigins`, resolved per run inside `ObservedReplayAuthorization.job()` within the ordinary dispatch pass; `Launch3` carries `scope` instead of deriving it from an account handle; the observed adapter performs the same origin check (`secretOrigins` per ID; absent list ⇒ bound to no origin) and the same password-only rule — the published `passwordControl` guard replayed against `/two-passwords` or `/no-password` ⇒ `POLICY_REFUSED`, nothing typed; replay is model-free (both gateways silent). The `requireSecretOrigin` implementation in `playwrightAdapter.ts` is **not** what the test cites (removed by OBS-012A). [design §3 `replay-job`/`replay-ipc` rows, §4.3, §4.6 I-A2/I-A3; oracle SEC-6 replay row, C-1]

8. **AC-8 — No value reads on password controls (F-6).** `hasValue`/`controlValue` reads on `type=password` controls are refused in the observed executor (learn and replay) with `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED`; assertion failure text never embeds a password-control reading (`observed` omitted); a deliberately failing value assertion on a text control whose page shows the canary produces redacted failure text (C-14). [design §4.6 I-B5; security condition 6]

**Never logged — sink inventory**

9. **AC-9 — Backend sinks (I-B4, F-4).** A final `SecretValue` type wraps `char[]`, prints `<secret>` from `toString()`, has no Jackson-visible getter and is written only by one explicit writer (`JsonGenerator.writeString(char[],int,int)`) used by the two secret-bearing serializers (`HttpRunnerDispatchClient` body, guided `BridgeDispatch` builder) and replay `job()`, erasing after write; `RunJob.resolvedSecrets: Map<String,String>` and `text(resolved.secrets())` are replaced. The Vault read is parsed with a streaming `JsonParser` (`getTextCharacters`) straight into `char[]` — the secret path never calls `ObjectMapper.readTree`; bodies are published as `byte[]` (`ofByteArray`) and zeroed after send (test seams for both). Oracle C-5: with root and `com.citi.put.checks` at TRACE and every appender captured during a two-path controlled run (guided learn, observed replay), zero canary hits in logs, problem+json bodies, SSE frames, `/actuator/prometheus` and the `IdempotencyFilter` cache; `RunJob.toString()`/`SecretValue.toString()` print no value. Residuals (JVM `String` copies, Jackson/`HttpClient`/TLS buffers) are documented in the evidence file, not asserted. [design §4.6 I-B4, I-A2 read/write residuals; security condition 4]

10. **AC-10 — Runner sinks (I-B5, SEC-7, F-10).** A static test asserts `tracing.start`, `recordHar`, `on('console'` and `screenshot` stay absent from `studio-runner/src`. The guided mode runs a redactor built from the resolved values over stderr lines, journal diagnostic text and callback `errorMessage` (a test-only hook embedding the value yields `[REDACTED]`, SEC-7). Oracle C-6 uses the separately labeled mandatory native, injected and supplementary controls below. Callback free text is exactly top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage`; journal free text is a distinct per-session diagnostic JSONL file with a closed safe identity plus already-redacted text. `GuidedJournal` keeps its existing owner/consumption hashes. The separate diagnostic file has restrictive permissions and finite session record/byte budgets; consume/recovery never reads it, it cannot restore/retry/admit/publish, and diagnostic-write failure cannot change a determined verdict or completed success. Redact actual resolved/known values before truncation, interpolation, serialization, stderr, callback or file write, then enforce the character and UTF-8 bounds; never stringify a secret-bearing frame or raw exception wholesale. C-6 separates three mandatory controls. Authentic production failures/refusals execute through the sole isolated collector/CDP password primitive, privately capturing actual raw text at the declared volatile test seam; the current trusted native refusal is asserted code-only TARGET_CHANGED without released-canary content. Supplementary direct Playwright.fill /slow timeout retains every raw-canary-positive, safe-[REDACTED]-positive and no-canary assertion. The injected actual released-value Error executes the production GuidedRuntime diagnostics and proves redaction before interpolation/bounds, UTF-8/character and session budgets, callback/sidecar/stderr scrubbing and unchanged hash-only GuidedJournal. Native, injected and supplementary evidence are labeled independently and cannot substitute for each other. Actual sole-primitive in-flight timeout, cancellation and context/transport loss exercise truthful effect knowledge; a readonly prewrite refusal alone is not a timeout proof. For the actual Core-HTTP/PostgreSQL/compiled-child/browser join require zero literal/encoded canary hits in child stdout/stderr, relay output, step failure, manifest, callbacks, diagnostic journal, authoritative journal and parent log for all applicable controls; constructionally discarded output is verified as discarded at its actual boundary, never credited as a redactor output that was not produced. Parent DEBUG=pw:* remains absent from the child environment while the run proceeds. No second selector/fill/raw-value production channel is added. The original literal positive assertion that an authentic production password native raw error contains the released canary remains preserved as historically unmet; only explicit independent PO revalidation of this exact replacement supersedes it. All other historical native/injected/supplementary assertions, negative/positive cases and complete sink scans remain mandatory. Code-only native text alone, an injected hook, absent sink or a unit redactor does not close the joined C-6 oracle. [design §4 "Runner outputs", §4.6 I-B5; security condition 9]

### What the code does today (design §1, condensed)

Guided input kinds are `nonsecretText | destination` and require a value. `GuidedSourceClassifier` already parses `<secret ID>` and requires it declared but emits configuration references only for `var`; the change is emission, not parsing. Every guided start fails `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED`. `knownSecrets` is always `[]`; the collector merges/withholds and wipes on dispose; sanitizer bound 64 × 4096. The collector **never exports a password control as a node** — hence the node-free target. The ordinary dispatch pass resolves secrets at dispatch only, erases on every exit path, carries `secretOrigins`; it has no password-only rule and no login detection. The observed replay job carries `accountHandle`; V33 DB functions require account fields; `AWAITING_AUTH` is in the V30 CHECK. `translation.enabled` is dead unless set (two gates). No production guided data exists; publication and observed replay default off; the guided worker has no `CMD`/chart (OBS-009).

### Target flow (design §2)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports"
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight mayUse + exists, no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS} (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target={kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner pins exactly one visible enabled input[type=password]
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal), RELEASE audit row, BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → same pinned element re-proven in-world (attached, type=password, unique, origin, form.action), withhold BEFORE fill, fill via handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run (ordinary dispatch pass), same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```

### Trust boundaries in one paragraph (design §4)

The gateway sees IDs, never values (structural: the kind has no `value` field). The DB stores IDs, vault version identifiers and audit rows. The only value-bearing channels are `BridgeDispatch.secret` (guided, mTLS + RS256) and `Launch3/Execute3.secrets` (replay, the backend→runner hop that OBS-009 makes TLS with client-certificate authentication). Runner memory holds the value from the dispatch frame until `withhold` copies it into the private inventory; wiped at `dispose`/`stop`; no scratch file, argv or env ever carries it. The browser profile is a separate disk sink neutralised by the pre-written `Preferences` file and canary-scanned. Video shows masked dots only (password-only rule); a page that later echoes a secret in plain text is a stated residual. Runner free-text sinks pass a redactor built from resolved values. Transport gates G-1 (guided mTLS), G-2 (no real credential in Vault until every secret-bearing hop is TLS-authenticated) and G-3 (no scheduled secret-referencing run before production background/secret-use authorization sources exist) are OBS-009/OBS-010 items and are **not** closed by this story.

Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Guided completion retains conservative OK→USED and every non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for each actual linked consumed secret admission; trusted backend no-send and authentic unreached facts retain their separately proven REFUSED/NOT_USED paths. A generic ledger ACK_LOST label alone never establishes actual acknowledgement loss. The present closed guided wire intentionally cannot transmit every private prewrite/post-fill fact; this does not authorize guessing. Prior committed positive facts remain immutable. No BridgeOutcome.secretUse field is added in this scope; any future completeness extension needs a separate explicit Aria proposal, fresh PO revalidation and root release. Four distinct guarded no-decision variants are permitted (all four use release_seq=NULL; actual linked release sequences remain unchanged): (1) true guided declared-but-unreached has one unlinked terminal USAGE/NOT_USED with null outcome/release_id/admission_id/vault_version/coordinate_ordinal and no fabricated release sequence. Its source_reference_id is the exact immutable configurationReferences.referenceId, coordinate_step_id is the declared source step, attempt is session:actual terminal owner fence, and full session/principal/CSI/environment/test/secret scope is authenticated against the immutable manifest and hash. A semantic obligation occurrence or selected-plan ordinal is never an actual action ordinal. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. Outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates are null; no release sequence is invented. The durable names-only no-send receipt and absence row commit with the owner transition. Missing decisionFacts, missing FINAL, post-send/no-admission ambiguity or a crash after possible read is insufficient. Other pre-send decisions, including genuine resolved-but-refused values, retain actual linked RELEASE/REFUSED facts. Retry authority stays separate: only existing genuine Vault-outage or definite transport refusal can authorize fresh attempt/grant/CAS; an absence receipt never grants retry. No admission/version/decision/release is fabricated and no extra Vault read or send is made for bookkeeping. For an accepted observed declaration with no actual committed DISPATCH resolution and no existing usage summary, variant (3) also permits a terminal-winner NOT_USED summary when an actual locked QUEUED/CLAIMED-to-DONE transition and a separate durable names-only terminal settlement receipt prove that no dispatch attempt/admission/observed admission receipt or transport entry existed, that every existing secret-value provider path was required to commit its exact scoped read-entry before entry, and that this ID had no such read-entry at the serialized terminal cut. A no-read classification is justified only by that universally enforced committed write-before-value-read protocol, the fresh serialized terminal view and the winning zero-send pre-send transition, never by missing FINAL/decision/marker rows alone; actual physical read counts remain independent executed test evidence. Read-entry acquisition and terminal closure serialize on the same owner row; no read may proceed if its required entry fails, and no new entry or RELEASE may be appended after settlement. An expired claimant is not impersonated as a live lease owner. The terminal winner authenticates the accepted history locator, immutable revision/declaration, exact binding digest/attempt and full scope. Its receipt, history/ledger transition and all new summaries commit or roll back in one physical transaction; deferred per-leaf guards verify the actual owner row version written by that transaction. This terminal-only proof grants no requeue, refreshRetry, deadline, grant, admission, dispatch or send authority. Existing live-owned completed-resolution CLOSED/REQUEUED receipts and their outage-only retry guards remain unchanged. (4) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared secret with a durable exact-scoped read-entry but no committed DISPATCH resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME only with that same authenticated winning pre-send terminal transition and terminal settlement receipt. Null outcome/release_id/release_seq/vault_version/admission_id/source_reference_id/guided coordinates means no committed resolution, release or action identity, never zero physical reads or proven use/refusal. The accepted binding attempt_id is real and remains nonnull even when ledger dispatch attempt_id is absent. A read-entry proves possible provider entry only: it may precede a crash before the call or a real read whose decision was lost. Do not infer a Vault version or any of the six resolution outcomes, ACK_LOST, NOT_USED, REFUSED or USED from this marker or a terminal error label. Physically counted reads/sends and actual crash positions remain separate test evidence. Unlinked terminal identity is exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/declared secret, independent of timestamp, caller sequence, guessed ordinal or retention partition. Existing actual RELEASE links and immutable USED summaries always take precedence; never append an unlinked substitute or a second summary. Post-send/no-admission ambiguity stays on actual linked uncertainty and is excluded from the new pre-send proof. A dispatched declaration lacking its required actual RELEASE is a lineage defect requiring evidence/remediation, not permission to fabricate an unlinked row.  The separate append-only CLOSED-only studio_observed_terminal_secret_settlements receipt is distinct from studio_observed_no_send_decisions and never relaxes that live-owned completed-resolution guard. Before the state change, its database insertion guard captures and authenticates the actual locked pre-transition owner-row before-image and exact accepted binding/revision/declaration/scope. A caller-supplied preceding_state, terminal error label or insertion against an already-DONE row cannot establish this proof. After acquiring any waited-for owner lock, classify under a fresh authoritative post-lock read-entry view, not the stale statement snapshot. Terminal closure fences future read-entry, RELEASE and send; a provider call cannot proceed without its required committed exact-scope entry. Receipt, terminal history/ledger and all required summaries share the actual winning caller physical transaction. Deferred guards on each current/future leaf independently verify that transaction's actual terminal row version, exact locator/binding/attempt and complete declared-ID classification. Savepoint/subtransaction row-version behavior must be proven or prohibited; transaction labels or self-invoked proxy annotations are not proof. External caller rollback and injected receipt/audit failures roll back every write. All actual immediate-cancel, generic-close, pending-reaper and kill-switch terminal entrypoints must participate; admitted/running reconciliation settles authentic linked facts under its real terminal state matrix, never this pre-send unlinked shape. Request-only cancel, applied=0, stale or losing transitions append zero rows. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE guards cover receipt parents and leaves, with no DEFAULT partition, aligned bounded existing 12-month Q3 retention, bootstrap/pruner coverage, stable cross-month deduplication and owner-row→owner-advisory→event lock order. No self-FK may prevent approved expiry; a same-transaction row version is not permanent identity. For these two unlinked replay cases outcome, release_id, release_seq, vault_version, admission_id, source_reference_id, coordinate_step_id and coordinate_ordinal are all NULL; the real accepted binding attempt_id is nonnull. The original three-variant null-release_seq rule remains and also applies to variant (4). Validate bounded unique disjoint no-read/possible-read ID sets against exactly the remaining authenticated accepted declarations, after excluding authentic existing decisions and summaries; no caller-chosen omission or invented ID is allowed. Durable entry is only possible-read evidence; the receipt/SQL does not measure a physical provider read. Without universal write-before-value-read enforcement, fresh-view classification or authenticated terminal/no-send proof, completeness remains unmet: emit no guessed negative. Known actual releases keep all scoped links/outcomes/version/sequence checks and honest linked settlement, including immutable early USED. A late loser cannot append its transient resolution facts after another terminal owner won. Existing GUIDED declaration absence checks continue to exclude any prior consumption/decision/summary across retained fences for that exact reference. A prior same-reference USED summary excludes a new unreached claim, but must not mask a later authentic consumed admission: settle that later admission under its existing actual linked or consumed-no-decision owner/admission/coordinate identity, without changing the earlier immutable USED or fabricating an extra declaration summary. This is existing approved per-admission authority, not a fifth no-decision variant or a wire change. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE. Preserve all actual release locator/timestamp/scope/owner/attempt/sequence/admission/coordinate/secret/version checks, unique write-once LIVE_RECHECK revocation events, duplicate/concurrent summary refusal and cross-month timestamp-evasion defenses. Unlinked timestamps are retention locators only, never fictional release times. Null actual RELEASE/linked-USAGE outcomes, malformed or wrong-scope links and spurious absence/admissions are refused. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, existing partition/bootstrap/pruner and Q3 retention constraints stand. Actual C-11 controller crashes before resolve and after read/pre-decision, replay child kills mid-fill/missing result, final-callback/reaper/cancel/revocation races and positive USED/NOT_USED/REFUSED cases use real resolver/send counters, fixture keystrokes and PostgreSQL facts; retain all audit value-canary scans. A genuine unreached GUIDED declaration also requires positively proven zero secret-value reads and zero sends for that exact reference, no actual consumed admission, no committed decision/RELEASE and no prior summary under any retained owner fence; absent rows alone do not prove absence. Authenticate exactly one immutable manifest secretRef entry with matching referenceId/step/name/intendedSlot=fill.value and no value under the retained scope and manifest hash. Join retained consumption through proposal sourceInputId to authored-input provenance.referenceId, never whole-step/name guessing. Enumerate manifest.configurationReferences even before any plan is selected. All three unlinked no-decision variants use release_seq=NULL. Linked actual RELEASE/USAGE keep their authentic positive release sequence; LIVE_RECHECK retains its approved affected-release lineage without inventing another sequence. The append-only backend-owned studio_observed_no_send_decisions receipt is keyed by (execution_id, execution_accepted_at, accepted_binding_attempt_id), bound to the accepted binding digest/revision/full scope and actual winning owner, and carries only bounded positively not-entered-for-value-read declared IDs, CLOSED or REQUEUED disposition and its own timestamp. For replay absence, source_reference_id is NULL as are outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates/release_seq. Mark read entry before each existing value-read call; build the negative set only from the authenticated accepted declaration iterator and actual completed synchronous resolver/literal-verification control flow. Any ID with an actual decision remains linked. No crash or missing decisionFacts can manufacture the set. Guard from locked authentic CLAIMED/current lease with no dispatch attempt/admission/observed receipt/sendCommitted; receipt, audit and winning close/outage-requeue commit together or all roll back. A guarded database transition constraint or equivalent database-verified owner interface prevents receipt-only commit; caller flags are insufficient. Keep owner row→owner advisory→event lock order, cross-month deduplication and Q3 receipt/audit retention alignment. The receipt provides no refreshRetry, deadline, grant or CAS authority: zero_send_decision_attempt_id remains limited to real VAULT_UNAVAILABLE outage CLAIMED→QUEUED provenance, definite_refusal_attempt_id to authentic transport refusal. Post-send/no-admission ambiguity is excluded. Supporting receipts are the existing RunnerReport.steps[] objects, exactly {stepIndex,status,startedAtMs,finishedAtMs,durationMs,failure}; they gain no stepId, sourceInputId, secretId, admission or other wire field. Derive stepId and the secret consumer from the frozen accepted artifact.steps[stepIndex].stepId/operations and inputRecipes: fill.value.kind=secretRef, sourceInputId→inputId, matching recipe.stepId, intendedSlot=fill.value and configuration provenance.referenceName. Require an in-range unique ordered stepIndex, status=PASS, failure=null, an actual browserStartedAt, finite nonnegative nonnull timings, finishedAtMs>=startedAtMs and durationMs consistent with their difference under the existing receipt tolerance. Validate raw receipts before projection/rounding; missing, duplicate, regressing, failed, started-only, skipped or contradictory receipts cannot establish new USED. The authenticated parent validates child runId/attemptId/order/timings against its actual ready admission/profile/build before deriving the monotone positive snapshot; the backend validates mTLS callback path/execution, accepted history and frozen binding/revision/artifactHash/profile/build, current attempt/admission/runnerInstance, increasing runnerSequence and the scoped RESOLVED RELEASE in the winning RUNNING report CAS transaction. Applied=0, stale/late/losing reports append nothing; audit/report failure rolls back both. STARTED/PROGRESS keep outcome and evidence null. Payload reduction omits every newly unsupported positive when its PASS support is shed. Terminal negative/unknown settlement cannot overwrite a committed USED or append a second summary; a complete later cumulative report may recover omitted supported positives without another action/read. This exact §4.1 amendment governs I-C10 and C-11 references to §4.1: their historical two-variant and terminal-only summary prose is expanded only by the four guarded no-decision variants, the narrowly authenticated terminal-winner variant (3) proof and early verified replay USED above. The original impossibility of a replay terminal summary after possible read with no committed decision remains historically unmet; only fresh independent PO approval of this exact terminal shape supersedes that linkage demand. No historical assertion is marked passed by this mapping. The retained three-variant null-sequence clause covers the original variants, and variant (4) also has release_seq=NULL. I-C10/C-11 historical linkage and two-variant prose is governed only by the exact corrected §4.1 rules, including authenticated terminal-winner proof, never by a generic absence-of-rows inference. Old zero-summary observations after possible read remain retained as completeness gaps; future evidence must add the authenticated UNKNOWN summary without claiming the old zero-summary oracle passed. All original forced-retry/two-attempt, declaring-source-step, null/link/scope/fence/sequence/time/version negatives, append-only/retention, actual crash/kill/race/read/send/keystroke and table-canary assertions remain mandatory. The former demand for an actual action ordinal/release sequence where no action/release exists is historically unmet and explicitly superseded only by this truthful null/reference mapping, never marked passed.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:120:Binding user requirement (2026-10-09): secrets must stay safe for compliance, be used **only at the right moment**, and **never be logged**. Every invariant below is testable (oracle `C-n` in §7), cites the code it relies on (read 2026-10-09), names its story (§10), and states residuals plainly. "Verified" means read in code; "required" means not yet true.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:126:| **I-A1 Step binding** | A secret is filled only (a) at a step whose authored source declares `<secret ID>`, (b) in slot `fill.value`, (c) into the unique visible password control resolved by trusted runner code in the collector's isolated world, pinned at `prepare` and proven to be the same attached element at fill (§4.2, R1-1/R1-3; the model never sees a password node), (d) with an owning `form.action` origin inside `allowedOrigins` (R1-2) and on an origin in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`. *Guided proposal:* `GuidedProposalValidator.java:323-339` joins obligation → source reference → authored input, whose `sourceStepId` is the declaring step (classifier `:152-171`); runner `guided/runtime.ts:143` insists `input.sourceStepId === p.coordinate.stepId && intendedSlot === slot`; (c)/(d) per §4.2/§4.3. *Artifact/replay:* `inputRecipes[].stepId` is the declaring step; `validator/observedReplay.ts:261` already demands `input.stepId === ob.stepId && intendedSlot === slotOf(kind)` for `authoredLiteral` — extend identically for `secretRef`, and the executor re-checks at `perform`. *Retired:* the artifact-1 binding in `validator/references.ts:101-170` and `requireSecretOrigin` (`playwrightAdapter.ts:504-520`) leave with the compile path (OBS-012A) and are not cited as evidence for the single path. **Story: OBS-007.** |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:127:| **I-A2 Just-in-time delivery and scoping** | *Guided:* the value travels only in the `BridgeDispatch.secret` of the admitted fill, built after `consume()` commits (`GuidedDispatchService.java:80-100`), withheld before the fill, inventory wiped at `dispose()` (`browser.ts:452`). *Observed replay — decision: keep run-scoped delivery.* All declared secrets are resolved once at dispatch and shipped in the `/v2/runs` job body (`StudioDispatcher.java:320-322,501-506`; `protocol.ts:106-113`). Per-step delivery was evaluated and rejected: it would add a second secret-bearing channel (backend → runner per step) and a backend-driven step loop that the autonomous artifact executor does not have, require either holding values in the backend across the run or N Vault reads for one authorization decision, and the value would still sit in child memory from that step to exit. Residency shrinks from minutes to seconds at the cost of a new channel on a hop that is not yet TLS-authenticated (I-C8). Revisit only if Security requires it after I-C8 lands. *Scoping (verified):* never cached across runs — `Resolved` is try-with-resources and erased on every exit path including throw (`StudioReferenceResolver.Resolved.close()`; `VaultStudioReferenceResolver.java:129-135`); the runner parent wipes on success/failure/throw/drain/cancel (`runCoordinator.ts:45,332-357,946`); one forked child per run with an enumerated environment (`launcher.ts:260-264,387-388`) so concurrent runs share no process; the child receives `stop`, then `SIGKILL` of its process tree within `stopTimeoutMs` (default 5 s; `launcher.ts:422,489-494,309-315`). *Guided worker:* `knownSecrets=[]` and inventory dispose on `dispose()`, one browser context per session — but in-process browsers share one heap, so inter-session isolation is by `capacity` (default 1, `ownership.ts:101`); **required (F-10):** the mounted config asserts `capacity === 1` while secret fills are enabled, or the two-session cross-value isolation oracle must pass. **Residual (stated):** JVM `String` copies and JavaScript strings cannot be zeroed (`StudioReferenceResolver.Resolved` javadoc; `runCoordinator.ts:332`); the decidable property is that no live reference survives wipe and the child process exits. On replay the values are resident in the child from the `execute` message until exit. *Read side (F-4):* the Vault response is parsed into a Jackson tree and the value is a `String` before `toCharArray()` (`HashicorpStudioVaultProvider.java:349-360`). *Write side (F-4):* both writers build a whole-body `String` (`HttpRunnerDispatchClient.java:113-116` `writeValueAsString`→`ofString`; `GuidedRunnerClient.java:87-89` `canonical(body)`→`ofString`). **Required:** parse the read with a streaming `JsonParser` (`getTextCharacters`) straight into `char[]`; publish bodies as `byte[]` (`ofByteArray`) zeroed after send. Even then Jackson, `HttpClient` and TLS internal buffers remain a residual. *Disk:* browser profile (§4 table, F-3). **Story: OBS-007.** |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:128:| **I-A3 Authorization at release; no stale frame is ever sent; bounded post-release window** | *No stale frame (verified):* `mayUse` and the Vault read happen inside the dispatch pass immediately before `send` (`StudioDispatcher.java:320-355`); revocation closes `AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED` with no send (`:356-360`); a Vault outage releases the claim and the next pass re-resolves (`:361-367`); a retryable definite refusal returns the row to QUEUED with a fresh `attempt_id` and the next pass re-resolves (`:440-445`); an ambiguous send is never resent (`:447-453`). Observed replay uses the same pass (`:388-392`); v3 moves `references.resolve` inside `ObservedReplayAuthorization.job()`. Guided recovery has three real fault positions: live/fresh same-worker/context/proof `ADMITTED/count0` before consume starts reads0/sends0 and may win consume once, recheck current authorization/origin/evidence, resolve once and send at most once; committed consume/count1 before resolve yields `AlreadyConsumed` with zero reads/sends and no new read/resend; after actual resolve or ambiguous send recovery adds no read/send, erases transient scope, preserves known success/failure and records honest uncertainty for unobserved effects. Context loss cannot rebuild/replay a browser; no `WonConsumption`, value or frame is cached, and no read-and-discard manufactures a counter. `AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED` is backend/API-assigned: own dispatcher denial before send, or terminal runner `ERROR/CANCELLED` mapped only against actual independently recorded `revoked_at`; a runner-supplied cause never assigns it. Actual user cancel retains `ERROR/CANCELLED` precedence when both facts exist, with independent revocation audit. Missing trusted facts/control-network loss stay unmapped cancellation/uncertainty, with no invented cause. Completed `PASSED`, `FAILED`, assertion-failure and `LOGIN_REQUIRED` outcomes are never rewritten by later facts. Keep write-once `revoked_at`, unique `REVOKED_MID_RUN`, worst-phase/slow/lost-response proof and the ≤2 s including request/queue time plus one already-in-flight step residual, with no next-step typing. *Post-release window (F-2, stated honestly):* once released, a value stays usable by the runner until the run ends — replay children hold every declared secret from `execute` until exit, at most `total-runtime` (default 120 s, `application.yml:259`; run deadline 600 s, `:253`); the guided inventory holds it until session `dispose`. Today the control signal carries only cancellation (`ExecutionControlService.java:28-31`; `control-poll-interval: 2s`, `application.yml:297`; `reportClient.ts:69-83`), so a `mayUse` revocation or Vault destroy **mid-run stops nothing**. **Required:** a worker-side revocation sweep rechecks `mayUse` for every in-flight execution/session with a released secret at the control-poll cadence and writes a write-once `revoked_at`; `ExecutionControl` gains `revoked: boolean`, carried on the progress acknowledgement by the same path as `cancelRequested` (`runCoordinator.ts:67,460`); guided sessions receive `stop{reason: REVOKED}`. The run is cancelled within one control poll and an audit row `REVOKED_MID_RUN` is written. **Residual:** a fill already in flight when revocation lands completes; the bound is one poll (2 s) plus one step, not zero. **Required:** `RunJob`/`BridgeDispatch` payloads are built inside the resolution scope and never enter a retry buffer or idempotency store; the backend guided dispatch digest is computed over the request **without** `secret`, and the runner's replay map strips `secret` before hashing — today it hashes the whole body (`guided/transport.ts:72`; F-7). **Story: OBS-007.** |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:134:| **I-B4 Backend sinks** | *Verified today:* `HttpRunnerDispatchClient` logs only the execution id and treats the body as a persistence surface (`:26-30,95-96`); `HashicorpStudioVaultProvider` logs no value, body or URI (`:48-49`); the guided package contains **zero** logger calls; logback root and `com.citi.put.checks` at INFO, no request-logging filter, no tracing dependency (`logback-spring.xml:39-43`; `build.gradle.kts` has no opentelemetry/zipkin/micrometer-tracing); `StudioDispatchMetrics` tags `state` only (`:69`); SSE error text is runner-redacted (`RunnerReportProjection.java:495-499`); `IdempotencyFilter` caches **responses** only (`IdempotencyFilter.java:173-180`) and no response carries a value (`StudioSecretDto` has no value field). *Latent hazard:* `RunJob` is a `record` with no `toString` override (`RunJob.java:61`); an auto-generated `toString()` would print `resolvedSecrets`. Nothing logs it today — a convention, not a type. **Required structural control:** a `SecretValue` final type wrapping `char[]` with `toString() → "<secret>"`, no Jackson-visible getter, and a single explicit writer used by the two secret-bearing serializers (`HttpRunnerDispatchClient.body`, guided `BridgeDispatch` builder; replay `job()`), erasing after write; replace `RunJob.resolvedSecrets: Map<String,String>` and `text(resolved.secrets())` at `StudioDispatcher.java:501`; the serializer writes via `JsonGenerator.writeString(char[],int,int)` into a `byte[]` body published with `ofByteArray` and zeroed after send. `SecretValue` closes only the `toString()`/accidental-serialization regression class; it does not remove the read-side JVM `String` residual (F-4, I-A2). **Required test:** profile with root and `com.citi.put.checks` at TRACE, controlled login run on both paths (guided learn, observed replay), every appender captured; zero canary hits in logs, problem+json bodies, SSE frames, metrics scrape and the idempotency cache. **Story: OBS-007.** |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:135:| **I-B5 Runner sinks** | *Absent by construction (verified by grep over `src/run/*.ts`, `src/server/*.ts`):* no `tracing.start`, no `recordHar`, no `page.on('console')`, no `screenshot`. **Required:** a static test asserts those identifiers stay absent from `src/`. *Env:* `DEBUG`/`PWDEBUG`/`NODE_DEBUG`/`NODE_OPTIONS` refused at browser launch (`browser.ts:465` `DIAGNOSTICS_DENIED`) and guided worker start (`guidedMain.ts:17`); the child environment is the enumerated allowlist only (`launcher.ts:168,208,387-388`), so `DEBUG=pw:*` cannot reach it. *Error text:* the executor redactor is built from `knownValues()` which includes secrets (`executor.ts:93`; `childRuntime.ts:243`) and runs before truncation (`pageLocation.ts:20-26`); child stdout/stderr pass the relay redactor and a released relay drops output rather than passing it raw (`outputRelay.ts:2-13,33-34`). The `text-entry-equivalence` disclosure line was a suspected sink: it logs **role names**, not values (`playwrightAdapter.ts:680` passes `target.role, resolved` where `resolved` is `firstRole`/`secondRole`) — verified, no change. Playwright `fill` timeouts are wrapped (`:557,:901`) and their messages pass the redactor; whether Playwright's own call log ever embeds the argument is **not relied upon** — the redactor is the control. Guided worker: §4 redactor over stderr, journal diagnostic text and callback `errorMessage`. *Value reads (F-6):* the observed executor already excludes `password` from `controlValue` read types (`observationSanitizer.ts:36`); its `assert.hasValue` path and any failure text that embeds a last reading must not echo a page-supplied password-control value (the redactor scrubs known values only). **Required:** refuse `hasValue`/`controlValue` reads on `type=password` controls in the observed executor (learn and replay) with refusal `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED` and omit `observed` from assertion failure text when the subject is a password control. (The legacy `expectValue`/`inputValue` sink at `playwrightAdapter.ts:1033-1034,811-814` is removed by OBS-012A.) *Measured, not assumed (F-10):* the supplementary C-6 Playwright.fill fixture captures canary-bearing raw error before the redactor; the production isolated-CDP native and injected controls are separately labeled and retain their own actual raw/sink assertions. Video is masked by I-A1(c) — "masked dots only" is a manual OBS-009 gate, not an automated oracle; manifest/journal/callbacks carry IDs and codes only (`envelope.ts:41,56-60`). Browser profile disk sink: §4 table (F-3). **Story: OBS-007.** T2 clarification: free text is restricted to bounded redacted outcome.errorMessage and the separate diagnostic journal; GuidedJournal hash records stay unchanged. C-6 separates three mandatory controls. Authentic production failures/refusals execute through the sole isolated collector/CDP password primitive, privately capturing actual raw text at the declared volatile test seam; the current trusted native refusal is asserted code-only TARGET_CHANGED without released-canary content. Supplementary direct Playwright.fill /slow timeout retains every raw-canary-positive, safe-[REDACTED]-positive and no-canary assertion. The injected actual released-value Error executes the production GuidedRuntime diagnostics and proves redaction before interpolation/bounds, UTF-8/character and session budgets, callback/sidecar/stderr scrubbing and unchanged hash-only GuidedJournal.
